To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the space of motions which can be performed by humans is not the same as the space of motions that can be measured by sensors, and (b) the space of movements which can be performed and measured by a sensor system is a function of the sensor system.

(i) the space of motions is different for each user-sensor combination; (ii) originality is a useful and measurable metric for the evaluation of user-sensor systems; (iii) the space of motion primitives is a useful and general representation of the space of user-sensor motions; and (iv) the space of user motions can be used as a basis to evaluate the relative effectiveness of different user-sensor systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a systematic and general method of establishing a set of movements suitable for use with any sensor system.
the development of techniques to evaluate the suitability of different sensor systems for the recognition of user movements, and to use this evaluation in the design of gesture lexicons.
the problem of establishing a set of gestures for a sensor system, and how the resulting gesture space can be used for the analysis of different user-sensor systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have demonstrated that the proposed method can be successfully used to create a set of motions which are both original and performable by users.

the proposed method provides a systematic approach to the design of gesture lexicons, and can be used to objectively evaluate the relative performance and limitations of joint user-sensor combinations.
this paper is the first to show how to create a joint space of motion that is both user and sensor specific.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the space of motions that can be used with a particular sensor system is limited, and that it is possible to use the space of motions itself to evaluate the performance of different sensors and different user interfaces.
it is possible to use reinforcement learning to create an original motion space that can be used for a variety of applications.
we have developed an algorithm to reward the originality of a user’s motion in a joint user-sensor space.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it provides a systematic way to explore the joint user-sensor space, by using reinforcement learning to reward originality, and to evaluate the performance of different joint human-sensor systems.
the originality metric can provide a useful and objective way to evaluate the performance of different user-sensor systems.
it is possible to use reinforcement to induce exploration of a motion space, and that this exploration is constrained only by the limitations of the sensors and humans.
